page: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Epsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by Microsoft's ARM Neoverse-N2 processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The CPU architecture is arm64, with each core hosting a single thread. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 128 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier memory bandwidth, with read-only large block speeds reaching 436.06 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 184.19 GB/sec. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 66283.59 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 19664.0. Database operations are highly efficient, scoring in the top tier on PassMark database tests with 37163.36 operations. However, single-core performance remains average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1661.0. Large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with prompt processing for a 70B model dropping to a poor 4.66 tokens/sec.

Given its ARM architecture and high memory density, the E32ps_v6 offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading. The absence of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, allowing users to scale Premium Storage independently. This configuration is recommended for memory-optimized workloads such as database operations, caching layers, and memory-intensive web serving. It is less appropriate for workloads requiring high single-threaded performance or large-scale LLM inference.
description: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v6 is an ARM-based, memory-optimized virtual machine from the Epsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by a 3.4 GHz Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor, paired with 256.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per core). The server does not include local storage or GPUs but is Premium Storage capable. Performance benchmarks highlight top-tier memory bandwidth, with large-block read speeds of 436.06 GB/sec and write speeds of 184.19 GB/sec, alongside strong multi-core processing capabilities. Conversely, single-core performance and large-scale LLM inference are average to poor. This hardware profile is optimized for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and high-throughput web serving where dedicated physical cores and high memory density provide qualitative cost efficiencies over traditional x86 architectures.
